STEP 4-5 - the words
widgets_values:
**STEP 4 (green)** fills itself from the queue slot you're working on -
don't type here, type in the queue panel's right box.

Write what MOVES, not what the picture looks like (that's already set by the
picture). Good: "she leans forward, lips part, slow breath". Bad: "red hair,
freckles" (the picture already has those).

**STEP 5 (red)** is the "don't do this" list - mainly "static / frozen" so
you actually get movement. Leave it alone.

nodes.title: STEP 7 - make the motion
widgets_values:
**steps** - how many passes. **20** is fine for Wan 5B. More (30) =
slightly smoother, slower. Fewer (12) = faster, rougher.

**cfg** - how hard it obeys your words.
- **~3.5** = loose, more natural motion, may ignore some of your prompt.
- **5** = the default - obeys but stays natural.
- **7+** = obeys hard, can look stiff or over-cooked.
Left = free, right = strict.

**sampler / scheduler** - `euler` / `simple` works well for Wan. Leave them.

**control_after_generate**: `randomize` = new motion each Run. `fixed` = keep
the same motion while you tweak words.

nodes.title: STEP 9 - saving
widgets_values:
**STEP 9 - save + make it longer**

Every clip **auto-saves** to `output/freedom_video/` the moment it finishes - you can't lose one.

- **Set User Save Folder** -> pick your own folder (remembered in this workflow). **Save to my folder** -> drops a copy of the last clip there.
- **Format**: MP4 plays everywhere (default) / WebM is smaller for web / MOV is for video editors.

**Extend video length** -> sends the finished clip back into the queue as a **green slot** (its last frame + its saved prompt come along). Type any extra motion, Run, and the new piece is joined onto the end. Do it as many times as you want.

Picking **10 / 15 / 20 s** does this for you automatically - it makes the clip in ~5-second pieces and joins them. Each piece is a few minutes, so a 20-second clip is a long wait.

nodes.title: READ ME FIRST
widgets_values:
## How to make videos

1. Make pictures in the **bigLust** recipe (the other tab). In its
   Preview & Pick panel, click the picture(s) you want, then click
   **Send to Video Queue**.
2. Come to this tab. Your pictures are now in **THE QUEUE** (the 9 boxes on
   the left).
3. Click a slot. In the RIGHT prompt box, type what should MOVE - e.g.
   "she slowly turns her head and smiles, hair sways, she breathes".
   Each slot has its own prompt. Empty = no motion words, the model guesses.
   The **Copy from previous prompt** button re-uses the last one.
4. Pick a **size** and **length** with the preset buttons (or leave the
   defaults).
5. Press **Run** (top right). If **Auto-start** is ticked, sending images
   already pressed Run for you. The queue works through the slots one by one.
6. Each finished video **auto-saves** to `output/freedom_video/`. To also
   drop a copy in your own folder, use **Set User Save Folder** then
   **Save to my folder** on STEP 9.

Video is slow on a 12 GB card - a 5-second clip is a few minutes. That's
normal.

nodes.title: STEP 2 - the LoRA add-on  (read this)
widgets_values:
**A LoRA is a small file that teaches the model ONE thing** - a camera
move, a facial expression, a body motion. You stack it on top of Wan here.

**This box is OFF right now** (orange, greyed) because you have no Wan
motion LoRAs yet. To turn it on:
1. Get one (see `comfyui_ext/LORA_SOURCES.md`, the **Video motion LoRAs**
   section - and mind the Base model: `Wan Video 2.2` works here, an
   `SDXL`/`Pony` expression LoRA goes on the bigLust IMAGE step instead). Drop the `.safetensors` in the loras folder.
2. Right-click this box -> **Mode -> Always**.
3. Choose the file in **lora_name**.
4. Put the LoRA's **trigger word** into your motion prompt (it's on the
   download page).

### strength_model  -  the "how hard it pushes" dial
Think volume knob: **left = subtle, right = strong, too far right = broken.**
- **0.0**  - off, nothing happens.
- **~0.5** - a gentle hint. Use this if the LoRA melts the face or warps
  the body.
- **1.0**  - normal full amount. **Start here.**
- **1.2 - 1.5** - crank it. Only if the motion is too weak at 1.0. Higher
  than this almost always distorts the picture.
- **-1.0** - do the OPPOSITE of what the LoRA learned. Rarely useful.

Stacking two LoRAs? Add another **LoraLoaderModelOnly** box after this one
and keep each strength lower (~0.6 - 0.8) so they don't fight.

nodes.title: STEP 3 - motion strength (shift)
widgets_values:
**shift** controls how bold the motion is overall.
- **around 5** = calm, small movements. Use for portraits, talking,
  breathing.
- **8** = the default - a good balance.
- **10 - 12** = big, dramatic motion. Use for action. Too high = jittery
  or morphing.

Left = calm, right = wild.

nodes.title: green slots = from a video
widgets_values: **Green-framed slots** in the queue came from a video (via Extend, or the **Load a video to extend** button). They carry the video's own saved motion prompt - click one and it shows in the right prompt box, ready to edit. When a green slot runs, the new footage is **joined onto the end** of that video.
